description: Largest-remainder allocation with an ascending-ordinal tie-break (ADR-0002 §2.6). The first input is the total; the rest are the weights, one per part. Every case here sums back to the total exactly — that is the property the method exists to guarantee, and the vectors additionally pin which line receives each residual unit.

provenance.oracle: ADR-0002 §2.6, worked by hand in minor units. Each expectation is reproducible with integer arithmetic: multiply the total by 10^scale, take the whole units each weight earns, then hand the remaining units out in order of the largest fractional remainder.
provenance.contentVersion: n/a — engine vectors, authored against the ADR rather than against a content bundle

cases.oracle: 777 units, one line, no residual. The degenerate case, included because totality has to hold there too.
5 units over 3 equal weights: each line earns 1 unit with remainder 2/3, and the 2 residual units go to the lowest ordinals because the remainders tie. Sum 0.05.
1000 units over 3: 333 each, 1 residual unit to ordinal 0. Sum 10.00.

10000 units over 3: 3333 each, 1 residual. The comparison case is rate-application/quo-thirds-at-minor-unit, where dividing each line separately gives 33.33 three times and loses a cent — the whole reason allocation is a distinct operation.
Weights that divide the total exactly leave no residual, so no tie-break runs and the result is the plain proportion.

10 units over weights 1:2:3 gives whole parts 1, 3, 5 with remainders 4/6, 2/6, 0/6. The single residual unit goes to ordinal 0, which has the largest remainder although it is the smallest line. Sum 0.10.
Weights need not be whole: 100 units over 0.333:0.333:0.334 gives 33 each with remainders 0.300, 0.300, 0.400, and the residual unit goes to ordinal 2 on remainder rather than on ordinal.
3 units over 4 equal weights: every whole part is 0 and every remainder is 3/4, so the tie-break alone decides. The last line receives nothing, deterministically and on every replay.

100 units over 6: 16 each with remainder 4/6, and 4 residual units to the four lowest ordinals. Sum 1.00. Round-then-adjust-the-last-line would put all four on one line — the bias ADR-0002 §3.4 rejects.
A zero weight earns no whole units and has remainder 0, so it cannot receive a residual unit either. An exempt line on a document stays at zero.
The one case with no proportion and an unambiguous answer. A non-zero total over zero weights has no answer and is an error — see errors/allocate-non-zero-total-over-zero-weights.
The mirror of ten-across-three-equal-lines. A credit note allocates exactly as the invoice it reverses did, so the two net to zero line by line; that only holds if allocation is symmetric about zero.

The total is rounded once, under the policy, to 10.01 = 1001 units, and the split is exact integer work from there: 500 each with 1 residual unit to ordinal 0. The parts sum to the rounded total, not to the unrounded input — which is what ADR-0002 §2.6 means by distributing a rounded total.
JPY at scale 0: 100 units over weights 1:1:3 divides exactly, so no residual arises. Allocation at scale 0 distributes whole units of currency.
100000000 units over 3: 33333333 each and 1 residual unit. The residual is one minor unit whatever the magnitude of the total — largest-remainder does not accumulate error with size.
